issue.title: `secp256k1_ecdsa_signature_parse_der` mangles overflowing R/s values rather than rejecting them
issue.body:
This issue is more minor than it might sound from the title.  (Maybe it's even "not a bug" but I want  to check.)

Consider the signature `304402206b5c3b1c86748dcf328b9f3a65e10085afcf5d1af5b40970d8ce3a9355e06b5b0220cdbdc23e6d3618e47056fccc60c5f73d1a542186705197e5791e97f0e6582a3201` from transaction `70f7c15c6f62139cc41afa858894650344eda9975b46656d893ee59df8914a3d`. This is a badly-encoded signature because there is an overflowing `s` value, but the `parse_der_lax` function that Core uses accepts it, and in fact it validates and the transaction  passes.

**However**, our `secp256k1_ecdsa_signature_parse_der` "parses" the  signature as one where the `s` value is 0, which then fails validation. (See `secp256k1_der_parse_integer` where on overflow we zero out the return  value, then return success.) This means that a user trying to call `parse_der` then "falling back" to `parse_der_lax` will reject the signature. More generally, the API provides no way for users to determine whether a signature that fails to validate failed because it's actually a bad sig,,or becasue it violates the BIP66 rules.

Maybe this is a non-goal of the API (or maybe it's a goal but nobody wants to touch consensus code to fix it), but it feels weird to me that the existing parser sometimes "parses" a signature into something that doesn't resemble the original signature. At the very least we should document this.

See https://git.rust-bitcoin.org/rust-bitcoin/rust-secp256k1/issues/1010 (or don't, because that issue is pretty sloppy).
